subject: Surge lanes & APAC micro-region dedicated pool request for Trilogy AI onboarding
messages:
From: Kelsey Tran <kelsey@trilogyai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Surge lanes & APAC micro-region dedicated pool request for Trilogy onboarding

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Tril ogy is excited to move fast. We expect to roll users into a beta in APAC starting mid-Oct and would like Redwood to stand up a dedicated APAC micro-region pool with tri-region fallback (US/EU) for latency-sensitive calls. High level asks: 

- Target go-live: 2028-10-18 (beta, then ramp over 8 weeks)
- Peak concurrency estimate (customer-side): ~180-220 requests/sec during peak windows
- Typical response size: ~700-1,200 tokens (mixed shorten/long chat turns)
- SLO: p95 latency < 300ms for streaming starts; throughput sustain during peak windows
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + VPC peering; we'll need audit log retention 12 months

We attached a completed capacity input form and an initial usage forecast. Can you run a region-aware sizing proposal (APAC primary, EU/US as fallback) + pricing for reserved capacity (monthly) and suggested canary plan? Also include suggested GPU class (H100 vs A100 or quantized alternatives) and a burst lane plan if committed capacity will be temporarily exceeded.

Attachment: trilogy_capacity_input_form.xlsx (xlsx, 110KB)

Appreciate a short proposal by EOD Friday if possible.

—Kelsey
Kelsey Tran
Head of Ops, Trilogy AI
kelsey@trilogyai.com

Thanks Kelsey — looping in infra sizing (Irene), capacity/ops (Ben) and sales CS (Naomi) to convert this into a concrete plan. Quick asks for the internal owners: 

1) Irene: can you run a 3-tier sizing (conservative/expected/peak) for APAC primary + minimal EU/US fallback based on the attached numbers? Please include GPU class tradeoffs (H100 vs A100 vs int8 quantized profile) and an estimate of tokens/sec per GPU we should use for each profile.

2) Ben: assuming we land on an expected sizing, what are procurement lead times for reserved capacity in APAC (spot/surge/backstop options + monthly commit pricing) and recommended contract tranches? Include an emergency temporary burst lane pricing for +30% capacity.

3) Naomi: please prepare a short mutual action plan and timeline we can send to Trilogy (SOW, security checklist, canary schedule).

I'll aim to consolidate inputs and deliver a customer-facing one-pager. Irene — if you can get a first cut today/tomorrow that would help.

Jordan Blake

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 8 Aug 2028 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Surge lanes & APAC micro-region dedicated pool request for Trilogy onboarding

Jordan / team / Kelsey — first-pass sizing below. I used the forecast values from trilogy_capacity_input_form.xlsx and assumed the model family is a 70B-class chat transformer (float16 production) with streaming enabled. Numbers are intentionally conservative; I'll attach the workbook with the calculation sheet.

Assumptions (from input):
- Peak requests/sec (Rps_peak): 220 Rps
- Median tokens per response (T_med): 900 tokens
- Peak tokens/sec = Rps_peak * T_med = 220 * 900 = 198,000 tokens/sec

Throughput estimates per GPU (sustained, with Redwood runtime batching & KV caching):
- H100 (fp16): ~30,000 tokens/sec per GPU (good batch efficiency)
- A100 (fp16): ~20,000 tokens/sec per GPU
- H100 int8/qat-like quantized path: ~45,000 tokens/sec (model-dependent, reduced quality risk testing recommended)

Sizing calc (simple ceil):
- H100 baseline: ceil(198,000 / 30,000) = 7 GPUs -> add 30% buffer for headroom/failover -> 10 GPUs
- A100 baseline: ceil(198,000 / 20,000) = 10 GPUs -> +30% -> 13 GPUs
- Quantized H100 baseline: ceil(198,000 / 45,000) = 5 GPUs -> +30% -> 7 GPUs

Recommended tri-tier proposal for APAC primary (with EU/US fallback each sized smaller for DR):
- Conservative (cost-optimized): 7 quantized-H100 equiv (burst on demand)
- Expected (balanced perf/cost): 10 H100 (fp16) reserved in APAC; EU/US fallback: 3 GPUs each (A100 or H100 small reserve)
- Peak (guarantee low latency peak windows): 13 H100 reserved + 4 GPU burst pool (spot/backstop)

Canary & rollout: 
- Canary window (2 weeks): 2 GPUs APAC dedicated (same model variant) + traffic shadowing for real-user shape
- Ramp 3 weeks -> reach expected sizing by week 5 -> hold for 3 weeks then open for full production

Operational notes:
- KV / prefix caching expected to reduce tokens/sec by ~12-18% for Trilogy prompts once warm; we should include that in test plans.
- Streaming starts p95 target depends on start-of-response token generation; quantized path may slightly increase start latency variance — recommend A/B during canary.

I attached the spreadsheet with the workbook derivation. If we want to be conservative on SLOs, use the expected tier with 10 H100s.

Attachment: trilogy_sizing_workbook_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 420KB)

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior SW Eng, Serving Runtime

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Surge lanes & APAC micro-region dedicated pool request for Trilogy onboarding

Thanks Irene — this is a solid first cut. A few procurement/pricing points and timelines from ops: 

- Lead times in APAC for reserved H100 capacity: typical availability turnaround is 6-8 weeks from signed commitment (can be expedited to ~3 weeks with a higher initial deposit + partner-backed inventory).
- Pricing (indicative monthly committed):
  * H100 reserved: $38,000 per GPU / month (12-month commit benchmark)
  * A100 reserved: $26,000 per GPU / month
  * Quantized profile discount: ~15% off H100 reserved pricing (reflects reduced runtime footprint & quota)
- Burst/backstop lanes: we can provide a managed surge lane priced at +45% over the committed GPU rate billed for the additional capacity used during the month. For a short-term emergency (<72h), rate can be negotiated per-case.
- Proposal of tranches: 1) Canary deposit + 2 GPUs pre-allocated (pay-as-you-go for 2 wks) 2) Move to expected tier (10 GPUs) with 3-month ramp commitment 3) Post-ramp: evaluate long-term 12-month reserved pricing if utilization meets threshold

Procurement checklist/risks: signed SOW + PO required for reserved commitment. SOC2 evidence and network connectivity can be staged in parallel with a 2-week security intake. If Trilogy needs VPC peering in a specific cloud region, we need to confirm account IDs and subnet ranges during intake.

I'll draft the pricing appendix into the SOW. Naomi — Jordan — want me to include the surge lane cost examples in the customer-facing one-pager?

—Ben
